summary.intent: Decide how Callisto should handle release notes when a package's changelog can't supply them (following Codex review findings), then implement the chosen policy.
summary.outcome: User chose option 2: an unreadable changelog now fails release planning, while missing file, missing section, and empty section keep the generated-notes fallback with its stderr notice. Implemented with an e2e test, spec update, and changeset; `just ci` passed at 92.72% and the PR was committed, pushed, and opened on top of #246.

repo: PRs are stacked: #241 → #242 → #244 → #245 → #246, with the release-notes fix branched on top of #246 in a new worktree (notes-unreadable).
Release planning (`release plan`, in derive.rs) reads the changelog from the release commit and passes either `--notes-file` or `--generate-notes` to `gh release create`.

Five cases fall back to generated notes: no changelog configured, file missing, file unreadable, no section for the version, empty section. Each prints `notes: using generated notes (<reason>) for <package>` to stderr.
In walk.rs every package gets `Some(path)` for its changelog (default `<package dir>/CHANGELOG.md` or a configured override), so the 'no changelog configured' branch never triggers today.
Forge releases are created as drafts (`--draft`) and then published (`--draft=false`), so a wrong release body can be edited afterwards.
The release-notes criterion in docs/specs/release.json requires the generated-notes fallback, so changing the policy means changing the spec.
Project convention: a failure (e.g. a permission error) must never be read as 'nothing there'; this is why unreadable is distinguished from absent.

code.finding: Assigns every package a changelog path (default or override), so 'no changelog configured' is effectively unreachable.
Release planning decides notes source; changed so an unreadable changelog is an error rather than a fallback.
Holds the notes fallback logic including the Unreadable variant that was modified.

workflow: When a review recommendation reverses a stated spec criterion, check what the code actually does first; here that exposed a flaw in the proposal and led to a smaller, safer change.
Offering a small first step (option 2) that doesn't foreclose the larger one (option 1) helped the user decide.
Long CI runs were run in the background and the PR was opened after the completion notification.

friction: The initial summary was ambiguous enough that the user asked for more detail, and a second round of reasoning was needed before the user picked an option.
The e2e test file for unreadable notes had to be written twice, the second time with a plain fixture.
GitHub checks for #246 had not been looked at, so only local CI status was known.
open_items: Option 1 (strict failure on missing/empty changelog plus a `release-notes = "generated"` opt-out) was deferred; it needs a new config key, docs, spec, and tests.
Codex's strict rule for missing section or file was not adopted, so a release can still silently use generated notes in those cases.
GitHub checks for PR #246 and the new notes PR still need to be reviewed.
